automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.policy: Only public sources with direct visible publish/update dates inside the window qualify; broad ecosystem entity facts are routed upstream and only local practice implications are retained.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub introduced Project HydraFusion as a Copilot CLI research preview that selects among single, cascade, and critique execution patterns; the design records cost, latency, role, diagnostics, cancellation, validation, isolated review, and fail-safe patch application.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It supplies a current public example of use/compose/build workflow selection becoming runtime policy, with bounded execution and isolated review as harness responsibilities rather than prompt wording.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: During ingest, keep broad product/model benchmarking upstream and synthesize only the local harness/governance pattern.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub described Copilot app agent sessions that run independently, keep their own context, and can execute in separate Git worktrees while the user monitors progress and reviews completed results.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It reinforces the local workflow rule that parallel terminal or app-based agents need isolated checkout state, resumable context, and review-centered human control.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use as practice evidence for worktree isolation and task review, not as a product encyclopedia entry.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub framed loop engineering as scheduled, repeatable agent systems with fetching, validation, escalation, skills, observability, routing, and checkpoints; it also described squads and fleets as role-specialized multi-agent workflow structures.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It gives public terminology for the wiki's scheduled feed and leaf-watch practices, especially validation checkpoints and escalation when a loop gets stuck.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: During ingest, preserve the local automation design implications and avoid importing the entire vocabulary explainer.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub reported that reducing individual tool outputs can increase total task cost when useful details are omitted, and described evaluating harness changes with complete task metrics and controlled online experiments before shipping.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It supports the local practice of optimizing automation and tool output for end-to-end completion evidence rather than local token count alone.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Good candidate for application harness and update-feed validation guidance; keep RTK details source-specific.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Help Net Security described ToolHive as an Apache-2.0 open-source platform that runs MCP servers in containers, applies permission files, identity/access policy, audit logs, registry curation, provenance verification, gateway SSO, traces, and metrics.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It is directly relevant to MCP server discovery and runtime governance: local practice should distinguish sandboxing from full identity, policy, and telemetry integration.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route broad ToolHive background upstream; retain the local governance distinction between isolated install and governed rollout.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Teleport argued that AI agent security needs unique agent identity, trusted runtimes with zero starting privileges, continuous behavioral enforcement, objective-aware monitoring, and runtime termination when risk is detected.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It strengthens delegated-authority and repair-gate guidance: point-in-time approval is insufficient when agents act continuously or in groups.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Treat vendor claims cautiously; useful as current public signal for identity and enforcement patterns.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Help Net Security reported Microsoft Project Zenith as a Windows 11 developer-PC experience with local large-model workflows and day-one platform protections for agents, including OS-enforced identity, containment through Microsoft Execution Containers, and enterprise manageability.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It shows terminal/developer workstation workflows shifting toward local model execution plus OS-level containment and identity controls.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep product/device details upstream; local implication is workstation policy for local agents.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Help Net Security covered Doppler positioning secrets management for developers, CI/CD pipelines, MCP servers, and AI agents, with a single system of record and runtime delivery instead of scattered credentials.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It adds a current public example that delegated authority must account for automated identities and runtime secret delivery, especially around MCP servers.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Sponsored source; use only as market signal for automated identity/secrets pressure.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Axios reported that U.S. Representatives Josh Gottheimer and Mike Lawler introduced the Stop Rogue AI Act, directing NIST to develop standards for secure AI-agent deployment, action verification, reliability evaluation, tamper-proof logs, and machine-readable agent inventories.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It is a public policy signal for inventory, auditability, and action verification becoming expected controls for delegated agents.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Retain local control implications; route bill tracking and policy background upstream if maintained there.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Axios reported Bugcrowd CEO Dave Gerry's warning that enterprise AI agents may become both attack targets and insider-threat-like actors, and that companies will need better visibility into agents, their actions, and controls around what exists on their networks.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It reinforces the need for delegated-authority inventories, attribution evidence, and security repair gates that can detect compromised or drifting agents.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use as risk evidence; avoid repeating sensational incident detail without primary-source corroboration.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Express Computer reported Zoho Catalyst 3.0 as an AI-agent-ready cloud development platform with AI IDE integrations, Agent Skills, MCP support, a non-interactive CLI, open-sourced skills/SDK/CLI/Slyte framework components, and hosting/runtime services.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It is a current public example of enterprise builder workflows exposing agent skills, CLI operations, and deployment surfaces that coding assistants can use from the development environment.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Pair with Financial Express September 2 article if ingest needs an independent source for prompt-to-production framing.
